analysis: The code flow: checkNotNull(keyFunction) ensures keyFunction is non-null, then iterates over values, for each value computes key via keyFunction.apply(value) and puts into builder, finally builder.build(). Potential runtime exceptions: NullPointerException from checkNotNull if keyFunction null, from values.next() if values contains null elements (documented), from keyFunction.apply if returns null (causes put(null, value) to throw NullPointerException). From called functions: builder.put (via arraycopy) may throw IndexOutOfBoundsException or NullPointerException; builder.build (via getKey) may throw IllegalStateException. These exceptions are either part of the method's documented contract (NullPointerException) or extremely unlikely internal errors (IndexOutOfBoundsException, IllegalStateException). No need to catch them in this snippet as they would either be intended behavior or indicate bugs that should propagate. The missing IllegalArgumentException for duplicate keys is a logic issue, not an exception handling gap. Therefore, no optimization is required.
